23:42.sourceText: καὶ ἔλεγεν Ἰησοῦ, μνήσθητί μου ὅταν ἔλθῃς εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν σου.
23:42.targetText: and he said to Jesus, “Remember me, Lord, when You may come in Your kingdom”;

groups.note: Both pinned N1904 analyses mark Ἰησοῦ as vocative, directly naming the addressed Jesus. English relocates that same name into the narrated to-Jesus recipient phrase; TR has dative τῷ Ἰησοῦ and an additional Lord vocative. No dative N1904 name or different addressee is invented.

Actual εἰς with accusative kingdom gives the into-kingdom phrase, whereas TR has ἐν with dative kingdom. English uses in with come; the complete governed place/kingdom phrase remains paired while the actual preposition/case difference stays explicit.

unmappedTarget.reason: TR explicitly adds κύριε as an address after remember me. Pinned N1904 instead directly addresses Jesus earlier and has no independent Lord title; the distinct name and added title are not given a false lexical identity.

23:43.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἀμήν σοι λέγω, σήμερον μετ’ ἐμοῦ ἔσῃ ἐν τῷ Παραδείσῳ.
23:43.targetText: and Jesus said to him, “Truly I say to you, today you will be with Me in Paradise.”

unmappedTarget.reason: TR explicitly adds the Jesus subject here. N1904 has said to him without independently repeating Jesus; the previous verse’s addressed name is not borrowed into this distinct speaking clause.

23:44.sourceText: Καὶ ἦν ἤδη ὡσεὶ ὥρα ἕκτη καὶ σκότος ἐγένετο ἐφ’ ὅλην τὴν γῆν ἕως ὥρας ἐνάτης
23:44.targetText: And it was, as it were, the sixth hour, and darkness came over all the land until the ninth hour,

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 explicitly prints ἤδη already. LSV and checked TR omit this additional time adverb; English as it were corresponds to ὡσεὶ, not to already.

23:45.sourceText: τοῦ ἡλίου ἐκλιπόντος, ἐσχίσθη δὲ τὸ καταπέτασμα τοῦ ναοῦ μέσον.
23:45.targetText: and the sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was torn in the middle,

groups.note: Actual ἐκλιπόντος is an aorist active genitive participle from ἐκλείπω, expressing the sun failing/ceasing to shine. The primary Mounce entry explicitly attests this sun-darkening use at Luke 23:45. LSV follows TR’s finite passive ἐσκοτίσθη wording as was darkened; the same solar-light loss is paired without replacing the actual failing lemma, active voice, or participial form.
Actual μέσον is the middle expression in adverbial accusative use. English realizes its location as in the middle; no separately printed ἐν preposition is claimed.

unmappedTarget.reason: TR opens the finite sun-darkening clause with καί. N1904 begins directly with the sun-failing genitive construction and has no independently printed initial conjunction here.

23:46.sourceText: καὶ φωνήσας φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Πάτερ, εἰς χεῖράς σου παρατίθεμαι τὸ πνεῦμά μου. τοῦτο δὲ εἰπὼν ἐξέπνευσεν.
23:46.targetText: and having cried with a loud voice, Jesus said, “Father, into Your hands I commit My spirit”; now having said this, He breathed His last.

groups.note: Actual παρατίθεμαι is present middle indicative, as English I commit. TR instead prints the future παραθήσομαι; the pinned present form is retained.
Actual δὲ is a continuing/discourse connector here, rendered now. It is not the Greek time adverb νῦν.

Actual ἐξέπνευσεν expresses expiring/breathing one’s last. The complete English idiom realizes that single verb and its encoded singular subject; no separate Greek His pronoun or last adjective is invented.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

23:47.sourceText: ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ ἑκατοντάρχης τὸ γενόμενον ἐδόξαζεν τὸν Θεὸν λέγων Ὄντως ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος δίκαιος ἦν.
23:47.targetText: And the centurion having seen what was done, glorified God, saying, “Truly this Man was righteous”;

groups.note: Actual γενόμενον is the aorist happening/becoming participle. English was done describes the same event that happened, without claiming a Greek ποιέω doing lemma or an independently written finite passive verb.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.
Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

23:48.sourceText: καὶ πάντες οἱ συνπαραγενόμενοι ὄχλοι ἐπὶ τὴν θεωρίαν ταύτην, θεωρήσαντες τὰ γενόμενα, τύπτοντες τὰ στήθη ὑπέστρεφον.
23:48.targetText: and all the multitudes having come together to this sight, beholding the things that came to pass, turned back striking their breasts;

groups.note: Actual θεωρήσαντες is an aorist active participle. TR instead prints present θεωροῦντες, followed by English beholding; the actual aorist form remains unchanged.

The actual definite breasts phrase is the body part struck by this same crowd in the immediately governing striking action. English makes that intrinsic ownership explicit as their breasts; N1904 prints no independent possessive here, while TR adds ἑαυτῶν. No separate Greek possessive identity is invented.

23:49.sourceText: εἱστήκεισαν δὲ πάντες οἱ γνωστοὶ αὐτῷ ἀπὸ μακρόθεν, καὶ γυναῖκες αἱ συνακολουθοῦσαι αὐτῷ ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας, ὁρῶσαι ταῦτα.
23:49.targetText: and all His acquaintances stood far off, and women who followed Him from Galilee, beholding these things.

groups.note: Actual εἱστήκεισαν is pluperfect active; English stood uses the same standing predicate without changing the pinned tense.

Actual αὐτῷ is dative, identifying the person to whom these people are known. English realizes that same acquaintance relationship as His acquaintances; TR uses genitive αὐτοῦ. No genitive form is substituted for the actual dative.

Actual συνακολουθοῦσαι is a present active following-together participle. TR instead has an aorist following participle, while English uses followed. The actual present participial form and compound lemma remain intact.

23:50.sourceText: Καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ ὀνόματι Ἰωσὴφ βουλευτὴς ὑπάρχων, ἀνὴρ ἀγαθὸς καὶ δίκαιος,
23:50.targetText: And behold, a man, by name Joseph, being a counselor, a man good and righteous,

groups.note: Actual βουλευτής is a member of a council; the primary Mounce entry gives this council-member sense for Luke 23:50. LSV’s counselor is retained exactly and paired with that council office, not with an invented personal-advice verb or a different counseling lemma.

23:51.sourceText: —οὗτος οὐκ ἦν συνκατατεθειμένος τῇ βουλῇ καὶ τῇ πράξει αὐτῶν,— ἀπὸ Ἀριμαθαίας πόλεως τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ὃς προσεδέχετο τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ,
23:51.targetText: from Arimathea, a city of the Jews, who also himself was expecting the Kingdom of God, he was not consenting to their counsel and deed,

groups.note: Actual συνκατατεθειμένος is a perfect middle/passive participle combined with the preceding imperfect ἦν. English was not consenting uses the same agreement predicate; no present N1904 participle is substituted.

unmappedTarget.reason: TR explicitly adds καὶ αὐτός to the expecting clause. N1904 has the relative who and the expecting verb, but no independently written also/himself phrase there.

23:52.sourceText: οὗτος προσελθὼν τῷ Πειλάτῳ ᾐτήσατο τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ,
23:52.targetText: he having gone near to Pilate, asked for the body of Jesus,

23:53.sourceText: καὶ καθελὼν ἐνετύλιξεν αὐτὸ σινδόνι, καὶ ἔθηκεν αὐτὸν ἐν μνήματι λαξευτῷ, οὗ οὐκ ἦν οὐδεὶς οὔπω κείμενος.
23:53.targetText: and having taken it down, he wrapped it in fine linen, and placed it in a hewn out tomb, where no one was yet laid.

groups.note: Actual neuter αὐτὸ names the body that is both taken down and immediately wrapped. English repeats that same shared patient in both coordinated actions; TR independently repeats the pronoun after the taking-down participle, but N1904 prints one pronoun in the wrapping clause. No second original pronoun is invented.

Actual αὐτόν is masculine personal Him, while TR prints neuter αὐτό and English resumes the body as it. The same deceased Jesus/body patient is retained under this person/body reference recast; the actual masculine pronoun is not relabeled neuter.

Actual οὐκ, οὐδεὶς, and οὔπω jointly express Greek negative concord. English realizes the single negative scope as no one yet; no independently positive source form or extra English negation is invented.
Actual κείμενος is a present middle/passive participle of κεῖμαι, the lying/being-laid state. English laid states that same placement-state without substituting an aorist τίθημι form.

23:54.sourceText: καὶ ἡμέρα ἦν Παρασκευῆς, καὶ σάββατον ἐπέφωσκεν.
23:54.targetText: And it was [the] Day of Preparation, and Sabbath was approaching,

groups.note: Actual ἐπέφωσκεν is the imperfect of ἐπιφώσκω, normally dawn/begin. The primary Mounce entry explicitly includes the near commencement of the day at Luke 23:54, supporting English was approaching here. The actual dawning/beginning lemma is retained, not replaced with an ἐγγίζω approach lemma.

23:55.sourceText: Κατακολουθήσασαι δὲ αἱ γυναῖκες, αἵτινες ἦσαν συνεληλυθυῖαι ἐκ τῆς Γαλιλαίας αὐτῷ, ἐθεάσαντο τὸ μνημεῖον καὶ ὡς ἐτέθη τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ,
23:55.targetText: and the women who also have come with Him out of Galilee having followed after, beheld the tomb, and how His body was placed,

groups.note: Actual ἦσαν plus perfect συνεληλυθυῖαι forms the were-having-come-together construction. English realizes it as have come with in the relative clause; the together/with sense belongs to the συν- compound and Him to the actual following dative pronoun. No Greek finite perfect or extra preposition is invented.

unmappedTarget.reason: TR adds καί in the relative description of these women. N1904 has no independent also connector in that relative clause.

23:56.sourceText: ὑποστρέψασαι δὲ ἡτοίμασαν ἀρώματα καὶ μύρα. Καὶ τὸ μὲν σάββατον ἡσύχασαν κατὰ τὴν ἐντολήν,
23:56.targetText: and having turned back, they made ready spices and ointments, and on the Sabbath, indeed, they rested, according to the command.

groups.note: Actual article and Sabbath noun are the temporal accusative phrase. English states its time relation as on the Sabbath; no separate Greek on preposition is invented.
